To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
AMP-activated protein (AMPK) activation induces vasorelaxisation in arteries from hypertensive animals, but the mechanism is not clear.

the endothelium is required for AICAR-induced vasorelaxations in both normotensive and hypertensive rats and the mechanisms responsible for endothelium-dependent relaxation are exclusively nitric-oxide-mediated in normotensive rats but are partially nitric-oxide-dependent and partially cyclooxygenase-dependent in hypertensive rats.
AMP-activated protein (AMPK) is activated in arteries of hypertensive rats and that activation of this enzyme enhances vasorelaxant responses to AMPK activators.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the role of AMPK in vascular function in health and disease.
the role of AMPK in the regulation of vascular tone in health and disease.
the role of AMPK in the control of vascular tone and its contribution to the pathophysiology of vascular disease.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

AICAR-mediated vasorelaxis in SHR aortic rings is endothelium-dependent and NO and COX dependent, but the COX-dependent component may be mediated via an AMPK-mediated suppression of COX-EDCF-dependent contraction.
the endothelium-mediated relaxation in the SHR is enhanced by AICAR due to a combination of enhanced NO and reduced EDCF production.
AICAR-mediated relaxation is enhanced in aortic rings from hypertensive rats, and this is due to an enhanced NO-dependent and COX-dependent component.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the AMPK activators, AICAR and metformin, are effective in lowering blood pressure in hypertensive rats.
AMPK-mediated vasodilation is present and enhanced, and is mediated via NO and COX in SHR aorta, and that the mechanisms responsible are likely to be related to enhanced AMPK activation in SHR aorta.
AMPK activation in the endothelium may contribute to the vasorelaxant effects of AICAR in the aorta of SHR, and may be beneficial in the treatment of hypertension and vascular dysfunction.
The main takeaway from our work is that
AMPK-mediated vasodilatation is enhanced in hypertensive arteries and that activation of AMPk may be a potential therapeutic target in hypertension.

the vasorelaxant response to AICAR is present and enhanced (in E(+) rings) in SHR, and this enhanced vasorelaxing response is due to a reduction in EDCF-mediated contraction, which may be due to increased AMPK activation in the vascular wall.
the AMPK activators may have potential as a novel strategy for the treatment of hypertension.
